title: Trace context test vectors
description: Shared by Agent Gateway, Agent Stream and Agent Watch. Each group tests one rule of the trace context requirements. Each case has a unique name, an input, whether the rule accepts it, and the exact expected output. A null in an expected output means the value is absent.

conventions.accepted: Whether the rule accepts the case's input, as the group's rule defines it. Every group has at least one accepting and one refusing case.
conventions.minted: An expected trace_source of minted means the appliance creates a new trace id: any valid id, so expected.trace_id is null and no parent span is set.
conventions.header values: Header values are given as the application receives them after HTTP parsing. null means the header is absent. An array gives a header that arrived as several header fields, in the order received.
conventions.delivery: A case of delivery_event_id or delivery_occurred_at has as input the JSON body of one webhook or stream delivery, and a shape: the appliance whose delivery it models (agent_gateway, agent_stream or any) and its wire. conforming is what a current appliance must send: event_id and occurred_at at the top level, the same two in an embedded audit record, and no timestamp. legacy is what an appliance not yet changed sends, which Agent Watch still reads and a current appliance may not rely on. nonconforming is neither, given to fix how Agent Watch reads it. kafka_headers, when a case has it, are the headers of the Kafka record that carried the delivery.
conventions.access_point: An Access Point case describes an Access Point with its Target at a direct address. An Access Point whose Target is reached over the Fabric (fabric://) is not described by these vectors in this version: it passes the caller's trace headers on as sent, as the contract's "Target classes" says.
conventions.target_class: fabric for a Fabric target (a request sent over the Fabric to a fabric:// target, as a Transit Point sends one, and in an Access Point case the Managed Agent at a direct address unless its Target is bound by external consent; an Access Point whose Target is reached over the Fabric is not described, see access_point), third_party for every other target, a Stream or Pay reached by a plain HTTPS address too, and external_consent for an Access Point's Target bound by external consent (consent_mode external), the exception to both: it gets the trace id in X-Gateway-Trace-Id alone

trace_id.rule: A trace id is accepted as exactly 32 hexadecimal digits in any case, or the hyphenated 8-4-4-4-12 form in any case, and is normalised to 32 lowercase hexadecimal digits with no hyphens. An id of all zeros, a braced id, a urn: id and every other shape are invalid.

span_id.rule: A span id, and a parent span id, is exactly 16 lowercase hexadecimal digits, not all zero. Any other value is invalid and is not written.

traceparent_parse.rule: A traceparent starts with a version: 2 lowercase hex digits and a hyphen, else it is treated as absent. Version 00 is valid only as 00-<32 lowercase hex trace id>-<16 lowercase hex parent span id>-<2 lowercase hex flags>, exactly 55 characters. Version ff is invalid. Any other version, 01 to fe, must be at least 55 characters, and its trace id, parent span id and flags are read as version 00 defines them, the flags followed by the end of the header or a hyphen. Neither id may be all zero. Nothing after the flags is read, used or written. A header that is not valid is treated as absent, and no part of it is used or written. The sampled bit is the lowest bit of the flags.

traceparent_compose.rule: The traceparent an appliance sends is 00-<the request's trace id>-<the appliance's own span id>-<flags>. An appliance always sends version 00. The sampled flag says whether the appliance recorded its span for export, and is the only flag bit sent: the flags are 01 or 00, every unknown bit set to 0. An appliance that exports spans sends 01 when its sampler recorded this span, else 00. An appliance that does not export spans copies the sampled bit of the traceparent whose trace it continued, and sends 00 when it continued none. An appliance composes it only from a trace id in its written form and a valid span id; otherwise it sends none. It composes one only toward a Fabric target; toward a third-party target it sends no trace header. Toward an Access Point's Target bound by external consent (target_class external_consent) it composes none either, and sends the request's trace id in X-Gateway-Trace-Id alone, as before the target classes: sent names what that Target gets. continued_flags is the flags of the traceparent whose trace was continued, as received, or null; hop, when given, names the appliance's route, and target_class the class of the target it sends to.

mcp_meta.rule: For an MCP request Agent Gateway forwards to a Fabric target (an Access Point's Managed Agent at a direct address, a Transit Point's target over the Fabric), it replaces a traceparent the request body carries in params._meta with the same traceparent it sends in the header, and adds none to a body that carries none. For one it forwards to a third-party target, it removes traceparent and tracestate from params._meta and leaves everything else in params._meta (body_other) as it is. For an Access Point's Target bound by external consent (target_class external_consent) it adds, replaces and removes nothing in params._meta, as before the target classes. hop names the route, target_class the target's class. accepted means the body's traceparent is replaced.

incoming_headers.rule: An Access Point, a Stream pipe, and a Transit Point without a verified transit token read traceparent and X-Gateway-Trace-Id; an invalid header is treated as absent, and so is a header that arrived more than once: none of its values is used or written to a record. Only traceparent: continue its trace, its span is the parent. Only X-Gateway-Trace-Id: continue it, no parent. Both, same trace: continue it, traceparent's span is the parent. Both, different traces: X-Gateway-Trace-Id wins, no parent, and a warning names both validated trace ids. Neither: mint a trace id, no parent. continued_flags is the flags of the traceparent whose trace was continued, else null; the flags then sent follow the traceparent_compose rule. accepted means a received trace is continued.

transit_point.rule: At an Agent Gateway Transit Point, a verified transit token sets the trace id and trace_source is transit_token. traceparent gives the parent only when its trace id is the token's; a header naming another trace is ignored, not refused, and raises no warning. Where the Transit Point requires a transit token, which is the default, a request without a verified token is refused and nothing is continued. Where it does not require one, a transit token that does not verify is not used, and the request follows the incoming header rule. continued_flags is as in incoming_headers. The trace id, parent span and trace_source are what the Transit Point's own records carry, whatever the target's class. What it sends its target follows the target's class (target_class): toward a Fabric target (a fabric:// target) it continues the trace, so sent names the trace id of the traceparent it composes (its own span and flags as traceparent_compose says), the same id in X-Gateway-Trace-Id, and the tracestate the tracestate_and_flags rule passes on; the receiving gateway continues that trace. Toward a third-party target it sends no trace header: sent is all null. sent is null when the request is refused. accepted means a verified transit token is used.

tracestate_and_flags.rule: When an appliance continues the trace of a valid received traceparent, it passes tracestate on unchanged and adds no entry, on every request to a Fabric target (for an Access Point, a Target at a direct address); a request to a third-party target carries none. When it starts a trace, or continues one named only by X-Gateway-Trace-Id, it drops tracestate. The flags follow the traceparent_compose rule and are 01 or 00, every unknown bit set to 0: an appliance that exports spans sends its sampler's decision; one that does not copies the sampled bit of the continued traceparent's flags, and sends 00 when it continued none. accepted means the received traceparent's trace is continued.

trace_termination.rule: On a surface that switches trace termination on (off by default), the Access Point keeps the request's trace id on its own records and sends a fresh trace id downstream to a Target at a direct address: in traceparent, in X-Gateway-Trace-Id and in the transit token. It writes one trace_terminated record whose trace_id is its own and whose downstream_trace_id is the fresh one, both in the written form. The outgoing traceparent names the Access Point's span. The fresh trace continued no traceparent, so its flags follow the traceparent_compose rule with no continued flags, and tracestate is dropped. accepted means the trace is terminated.

trace_source.rule: trace_source says where a record's trace id came from. Agent Gateway writes transit_token, header or minted; Agent Stream writes header or minted. Its link mark: transit_token is verified, header is a claim, minted has no link upward. Any other value, and a record without one, carries no mark.

link.rule: A path from a record up to the Access Point record that holds the original caller is verified only when every record on it below the Access Point has trace_source transit_token. It is a claim when any has header, or no mark, and none has minted. A record with minted has no link upward, so the path ends there. A model call's link is always a claim. accepted means the path reaches the Access Point.

caller_identity_verified.rule: Agent Stream's governance record and refusal event say whether the caller was named from a verified source, beside caller_identity_kind. A JWT claim, an mTLS certificate field and an API key's name are verified. A request header and a field of the request body are claims. A request with no caller has no value. accepted means verified.

caller_key.rule: Agent Watch groups an Agent Gateway caller by a stable key built from the caller object of its records: jwt_bearer by issuer and subject (sub; principal only when the token has no sub, because a principal can be an email), did_auth by the DID, api_key by the key's name, mtls by the certificate subject DN. The key is the method's prefix and its parts joined by |, with % written %25 and | written %7C inside a part. A caller missing a part has no key. The display label is the email, else the name, else none; it is never part of the key.

request_forwarded.rule: Agent Gateway writes one request_forwarded record (integration event type audit.request_forwarded) for each Access Point request it forwards, when it forwards it. A request refused before forwarding, a Transit Point request and a Fabric receive write none. request_id and span_id hold the same value. caller and caller_did are present only for an authenticated caller. The record carries occurred_at, the time the request was handed to its target, and no timestamp. The record never carries an identity hash, a request body, a header value or a token. accepted means the record is written.

transit_request_forwarded.rule: Agent Gateway writes one transit_request_forwarded record (integration event type audit.transit_request_forwarded) for each Transit Point request it forwards to its target, when it forwards it, whatever the route, over the Fabric too. A Transit Point request refused before forwarding writes none (it is a request_rejected), and an Access Point request and a Fabric receive write none. request_id and span_id hold the Transit Point's span id; trace_id, parent_span_id and trace_source are resolved as the transit_point rule says, the verified transit token first. It carries no caller and no caller_did: the original caller is the one on the Access Point's request_forwarded, reached through the trace. The record carries occurred_at, the time the request was handed to its target, and no timestamp. The record never carries an identity hash, a request body, a header value or a token. accepted means the record is written.

delivery_event_id.rule: Every webhook and stream delivery carries at its top level event_id: a UUID in its hyphenated form, fixed when the appliance creates the event and the same on every delivery and retry of it. An embedded audit record carries the same event_id. It is never sent in a Kafka record header. Agent Watch reads the top-level event_id, else, for an audit.* event, the event_id of its audit record (record, audit_record or data), as an older appliance sends it. A usable id is a hyphenated, non-nil UUID in any case; an empty, unfilled, nil or otherwise formed value counts as absent. When both are usable and differ, the top level wins. An id inside an event's state or in a header is not read. Deliveries with the same event id are one event. accepted means the event has an event id; expected.event_id is it, in lowercase.

delivery_occurred_at.rule: Every webhook and stream delivery carries at its top level occurred_at, the RFC 3339 time with an offset at which the event happened, and no timestamp. An embedded audit record carries the same occurred_at. Agent Watch places an event at the top-level occurred_at; when that is absent (missing, null or an unfilled variable), at the top-level timestamp, which only an appliance not yet changed sends. A value present but not an RFC 3339 time is never replaced by the other field: Agent Watch places the event at the delivery's own time (the webhook's X-Webhook-Timestamp or the Kafka record's CreateTime, else when it arrived), so expected.occurred_at is null. An event placed more than 400 days back or more than 5 minutes ahead is not recorded (outside_window). A time only inside an embedded record or an event's state is not read. accepted means the event is placed at a time its delivery states, and recorded.
